question: Should OpenClaw add a native context-pressure alert/recovery contract for child sessions, and should that contract notify only, wake the parent, or trigger automatic recovery?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior adds alert thresholds, parent identity, notification routing, and recovery semantics that current docs/config do not define and VISION.md constrains if it becomes a broad hierarchy framework.

options.title: Design narrow session-health contract
options.body: Add a bounded context-pressure signal for child sessions, choose one operator/parent notification surface, and defer automatic recovery until live proof defines the failure mode.

options.title: Fold into terminal-session monitor work
options.body: Treat this as a sibling of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91832 and first design one shared saturated-session monitor before parent-specific behavior.

options.title: Decline core orchestration semantics
options.body: Keep core to reporting/diagnostics only and ask operators to implement fleet-specific parent recovery through plugins or external monitoring.

recommendation.title: Design narrow session-health contract
recommendation.body: Add a bounded context-pressure signal for child sessions, choose one operator/parent notification surface, and defer automatic recovery until live proof defines the failure mode.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice crosses session-health, diagnostics, and VISION.md orchestration boundaries, and current source history points to steipete on the relevant lines.
